title: feat(pm): derive check:type-check-debt for the ROOT tsc program, whose scope no path literal can describe
body:
Fixes #9873

Derives `check:type-check-debt` for the one gate population in the tree that no path literal can describe: the ROOT package's tsc program, declared by **exclusion** in `tsconfig.json`, so "everything else" has no positive spelling.

## Reproduction — before and after, same command

The exact path from PR #9853, the card that paid for this:

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs scripts/bench/runtime-publish-gate.bench.mts
```

| | names `check:type-check-debt`? |
|---|---|
| **before** | no — 2 gates, both `cross-package-test-inputs`; the ratchet scores `silent` |
| **after** | yes — new convention section, with the repair direction and the build prerequisite |

**Positive control** (the "names nothing" claim is not vacuous): the same command on `scripts/check-test-typecheck.mts` — the one *measured* coupling constant — names `check:type-check-debt` on **both** sides. The gate was always reachable; it named exactly one root-program path, which is the design this card engages.

## Why this does not weaken the gate's measured-couplings discipline

`check-type-check-coverage.mjs:357-363` states this card's own thesis, in the gate author's words, before the card existed — and refuses an automatic rule because *"an automatic rule would register couplings nobody has measured"*. That reasoning is engaged, not routed around:

**The two lists answer different questions, and only one is a measurement.**

- The gate's ledger records **magnitude**. `ROOT_PROGRAM_COUPLED_SCRIPT` does not merely say "this file is in the program" — it carries a measured claim (that file is 29 of the entry's 80 errors) and the ledger note spends that number. A rule manufacturing such constants automatically really would register unmeasured couplings.
- `CHANGE_KIND_GATES` records **relevance** — which gate a seat is told to run before pushing. That needs no measurement to be true: it is already settled by a file the repo maintains for another purpose. A path is in the root program when the root tsconfig does not exclude it.

This PR adds **no constant, moves no count, asserts no magnitude**. `ROOT_PROGRAM_COUPLED_SCRIPT` and all of its references are untouched, and its self-test pin still passes. This is triage's **option 1**, which triage named as the compatible shape for exactly this reason.

`scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` is **not modified by this PR.**

## Read, never mirrored

The excluded directories come from `tsconfig.json`'s own `exclude` array at runtime, not a hand-written copy — a copy would be the "second contract that agrees until one side moves" this file's i18n entries were rewritten to remove. Unparseable config or missing `exclude` **throws** rather than degrading to "excludes nothing", which would fire the kind on every TS file in the tree.

## The extension test is load-bearing, not tidy

The root config sets no `allowJs`, so JavaScript in those same directories is **outside** the program:

| in these directories | count | in the root program? |
|---|---|---|
| tracked `.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` (nearly all checker scripts) | 117 | no |
| tracked `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts` | 11 | **yes** |

A bare "outside those directories" test would fire on **128 paths to reach 11**, sending every card that edits a checker script to a ratchet that needs a built workspace closure. The new entry fires on **11 of 6107 tracked files (0.18%)** — and that population corroborates the ledger note's own accounting, which attributes 29 errors to `check-test-typecheck.mts` and 32 to the `analytics-reconcile` tree, 6 of the 11.

## Known limit, stated in the entry rather than discovered later

Per the PM addendum: `exclude` drops files only from tsc's **initial walk**, so sources under an excluded directory that a root script **imports** are pulled into the program anyway — the ledger note records 4 of the 80 arriving that way from the showcase example. A path-shaped trigger cannot see an import graph, so a card editing *only* such a file is still not sent here.

Deliberately not closed on this card. The direction is the safe one (this **under**-covers rather than over-covers), and closing it means resolving the program *including imports* — option 2, a different tool than a path predicate. The entry's doc comment says so, with a stated deletion criterion.

## Verification

Union re-derived and re-run at final head `297a4042b`:

| gate | verdict line |
|---|---|
| `check:pm-dispatch-gates` | `dispatch-gates self-test: 421 cases pass.` |
| `check:cross-package-test-inputs` | `All 60 self-test cases passed.` / `OK: 12 package(s) read outside themselves…` |
| `check:nul-bytes` | `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 6102 text file(s) … no raw ASCII control bytes).` |

Self-test **398 → 421** (+23 cases). It caught a real mismatch on its first run (the `why` said `Shrink-only` against a lowercase anchor) before going green.

**Ablation** — three mutations, each confirmed on disk in both directions (removed-marker 0, injected-marker >= 1), restored byte-identically (sha256 match) and re-verified green. No rebuild is involved: this is a pure source module the self-test imports directly, with no `dist/` resolution.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| drop the TypeScript-extension test (pretend `allowJs`) | **4 red** — incl. `a checker script is NOT in the root program` |
| make the exclude read return nothing | **8 red** — incl. `a package source is NOT in the root program` |
| strip the baseline-raise refusal from the `why` | **1 red** — the repair-direction case |

**No hint leakage.** Prose in a `why` is a module-body string scanned for watch hints, which this file documents as a live trap. Residue verdict counts were captured across 10 representative paths before and after: **identical on all 10** — no family changed verdict. The only cross-tree delta is the kind's name joining the enumeration line.

**Lock:** these three gates are pure source-text scanners that exclude `dist/` from their walk and spawn nothing, so they were run **outside `os-verify-lock.sh`** while another agent held it — declared here per the dispatch note.

**Clause 2:** not triggered. Path limb (`packages/spec/src/**`) is not touched — the diff is one file, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`. Content limb: this is PM tooling that changes what a dev brief *names*; it alters no contract accept/reject behaviour and widens no public surface.

**Changeset:** none — root `scripts/` publishes nothing ⇒ `skip-changeset`.
